title: What you need

blocks.what_we_do: Prepare a computer, a project folder and the tools used throughout the course.
blocks.why:
R is the language that runs our commands. RStudio provides a console, file
browser and editor around R. PLINK 2 is a separate program that processes
genotypes. A genotype records the alleles observed at a DNA site. R starts
PLINK for you, but installing R does not install PLINK.
blocks.you_need:
A Windows, macOS or Linux computer; an internet connection for software and
the approved data download; and a writable folder. The local data test does
not require a network download. Keep space for the encrypted archive, an
extracted copy and intermediate results. Required space grows as you work.
blocks.command:
Once R is installed, this safe command identifies your operating system:

```{r s0-1_system}
Sys.info()[c("sysname", "release", "machine")]
```

Terminal equivalent: `Rscript -e "print(Sys.info())"`. `-e` evaluates the R
expression in quotes. Do not paste terminal commands into the R console.
blocks.expected_result:
A named list of system information: Windows, Darwin (macOS), or Linux, with
your own system release and processor. These values depend on your computer.
They are not genotype counts.
blocks.troubleshooting:
If `Sys.info()` is not recognised, check that you are typing in the R console,
which normally displays `>`. Continue with step 0.2 if R is not installed yet.
blocks.quick_check:
Does installing R also install the program that analyses the genotype files?

<details><summary>Show the answer</summary>No. PLINK 2 is installed separately at step 0.4.</details>
